concepts.name: OpenAI Agents SDK sessions for conversation history

questions.prompt: A test wraps `parse_reply(raw)` in `with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="rate limit"):`, and `parse_reply` raises `ValueError("Hit rate limit (429)")`. Does the test pass?

choices.text: No: `match` must equal the exception's whole message exactly
No: `match` is anchored at the start of the message, like `re.match`
Yes: `match` is a regex searched for anywhere in the message
Yes, but only because `match` ignores case and whitespace by default

questions.explanation: `match` is a regular expression tested with `re.search` against the string form of the exception, so it can match anywhere in the message. It is not an exact comparison, and it is not anchored at the start like `re.match`; use `^` and `$` in the pattern if you need that.

sources.title: How to write and report assertions in tests
sources.claim: The `match` keyword of `pytest.raises` tests that a regular expression matches the string representation of the exception, using `re.search`.

questions.prompt: Your MCP server can serve any of 50,000 support tickets, each at a URI like `tickets://{id}`. Which MCP feature lets it advertise all of them without listing every one?

choices.text: A `notifications/resources/list_changed` sent as each ticket opens
The `subscribe` capability, so clients receive each ticket as it changes
A resource template, listed with `resources/templates/list`
Pagination of `resources/list`, so clients fetch one ticket per page

questions.explanation: Resource templates expose parameterized resources through RFC 6570 URI templates, listed by `resources/templates/list`, and their arguments can be auto-completed with the completion API. The client then reads a concrete ticket with `resources/read`. `list_changed` and subscriptions tell clients about changes; they don't describe a family of resources.

sources.title: Resources
sources.claim: Resource templates let servers expose parameterized resources using RFC 6570 URI templates, discovered with `resources/templates/list`, with arguments auto-completable through the completion API; `listChanged` and `subscribe` are change notifications.

questions.prompt: Your OpenAI Agents SDK chatbot must remember each user's earlier turns across separate `Runner.run` calls. How do Sessions handle this, and what must you not combine them with?

model_answer.summary: A Session loads the stored history before each run and saves the run's new items after it, keyed by a session ID per user or thread; it can't be combined with server-side continuation options in the same run.
key_points: Before each run, the runner retrieves the session's history and prepends it to the input, so you don't pass `.to_input_list()` yourself
After each run, all new items (user input, assistant responses, tool calls) are stored in the session
Use one session ID per user or conversation, since different sessions keep separate histories; `SQLiteSession` with a file path persists, without one it is in memory
In one run, a session can't be combined with `conversation_id`, `previous_response_id` or `auto_previous_response_id`

questions.explanation: Sessions replace the manual pattern of feeding `result.to_input_list()` into the next run. The choice is between client-side memory (a Session) and server-managed continuation, not both: mixing them in one run is refused, and is the trap here.

sources.title: Sessions
sources.claim: Sessions retrieve the conversation history and prepend it before each run, store all new items after it, keep separate histories per session ID, offer in-memory or file-backed SQLiteSession, and cannot be combined in the same run with conversation_id, previous_response_id or auto_previous_response_id.

questions.prompt: Your code defines `class ToolArgsError(ValueError)`, and `call_tool()` raises it. A test wraps the call in `with pytest.raises(ValueError):`. What happens?

choices.text: It fails, since `pytest.raises` needs the exact exception type
It passes, since `pytest.raises` also matches any subclass
It fails unless you also pass `match=` with the error message
It passes only if `ToolArgsError` is listed in `conftest.py`

questions.explanation: `pytest.raises` matches the exception type or any subclass, like an `except` clause. That also means a broad type such as `ValueError` can pass on the wrong error; assert on `excinfo.type` or pass `match=` when the exact error matters. `match` is optional.

sources.title: How to write and report assertions in tests
sources.claim: `pytest.raises` matches the exception type or any subclasses, like the standard except statement; the ExceptionInfo it returns has `.type`, `.value` and `.traceback`.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list` and `resources/read` in MCP, and what a server must return when a client reads a resource that doesn't exist.

model_answer.summary: `resources/list` returns concrete resources, `resources/templates/list` returns parameterized URI templates, and `resources/read` returns the contents for one URI; a missing resource is a JSON-RPC error, not an empty result.
key_points: `resources/list` returns the concrete resources available, each with a URI, and supports pagination
`resources/templates/list` returns templates with a `uriTemplate` (RFC 6570) whose arguments can be auto-completed
`resources/read` takes a URI and returns its contents as text or base64 `blob`
A resource that doesn't exist gets JSON-RPC error `-32602` (clients should also accept the older `-32002`), never an empty `contents` array

questions.explanation: Templates let a server describe huge or open-ended sets of resources, like every file or ticket, without listing each one, while `resources/read` always works on a concrete URI. An empty `contents` array is forbidden for a missing resource because it is ambiguous with a resource that exists but is empty.

sources.title: Resources
sources.claim: `resources/list` lists resources with pagination, `resources/templates/list` lists RFC 6570 URI templates, `resources/read` returns text or blob contents for a URI, and a non-existent resource MUST get error -32602, with -32002 accepted for older versions, never an empty contents array.

questions.prompt: Your OpenAI Agents SDK service creates `SQLiteSession("user_123")` with no database path, and the process restarts. What happens to user_123's conversation history?

choices.text: It is kept in a default `agents.db` file next to your code
It is kept on OpenAI's servers under that same session ID
It is restored from the last `previous_response_id` used
It is lost: without a path, the session lives in memory

questions.explanation: `SQLiteSession("user_123")` without a file path is an in-memory database, lost when the process ends. Pass a path, as in `SQLiteSession("user_123", "conversations.db")`, to persist it. Sessions are client-side storage, separate from OpenAI's server-managed continuation, and can't be combined with it in one run.

sources.title: Sessions
sources.claim: `SQLiteSession("user_123")` is in memory and lost when the process ends, while `SQLiteSession("user_123", "conversations.db")` persists to a file.

questions.prompt: Your OpenAI Agents SDK chatbot must remember each user's earlier turns across separate `Runner.run` calls. Which statements about Sessions are true? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Before each run, the session's history is fetched and prepended to the new input
You still call `.to_input_list()` after each run and pass that in yourself
After each run, its new items (input, replies, tool calls) are stored
Use one session ID per user or conversation: each ID keeps its own history
A session works best combined with `previous_response_id` in the same run

questions.explanation: With a session, the runner retrieves the stored history before each run and prepends it to the input, then stores every new item (user input, assistant responses, tool calls) after the run, so you no longer call `.to_input_list()` yourself. Each session ID keeps a separate history, so give each user or conversation its own. Sessions are client-side memory and can't be combined in one run with `conversation_id`, `previous_response_id` or `auto_previous_response_id`.

sources.title: Sessions
sources.claim: Before each run the session's conversation history is retrieved and prepended to the input; after each run all new items (user input, assistant responses, tool calls) are stored; each session ID keeps a separate history; there is no need to call `.to_input_list()` manually; sessions cannot be combined in the same run with `conversation_id`, `previous_response_id` or `auto_previous_response_id`.

questions.prompt: An MCP server exposes project files as resources. Which statements about `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list` and `resources/read` are true? Select all that apply.

choices.text: `resources/templates/list` returns RFC 6570 `uriTemplate`s with completable arguments
`resources/read` takes a URI and returns its contents as `text` or a base64 `blob`
Reading a resource that doesn't exist returns an empty `contents` array, not an error
`resources/list` returns every resource in one response, since it has no pagination
A missing resource gets error `-32602`, and clients also accept the older `-32002`

questions.explanation: `resources/list` lists concrete resources and supports pagination. `resources/templates/list` lists parameterized resources as RFC 6570 URI templates, whose arguments can be auto-completed. `resources/read` returns a resource's contents as text or base64 `blob`. For a resource that doesn't exist, the server MUST return JSON-RPC error `-32602`, and clients SHOULD also accept the older `-32002`; an empty `contents` array is forbidden because it is ambiguous.

sources.title: Resources
sources.claim: `resources/list` supports pagination; `resources/templates/list` exposes parameterized resources as RFC 6570 URI templates whose arguments may be auto-completed; `resources/read` returns text or base64 blob contents for a URI; for a non-existent resource servers MUST return error -32602, clients SHOULD also accept -32002 from earlier versions, and servers MUST NOT return an empty contents array.
